comments.body:
PRE-IMPLEMENTATION RESEARCH — three corrections to this ticket, all MEASURED against the pinned
dependencies in this worktree (boto3/botocore 1.43.58, pydantic-ai-slim 1.107.1).

CORRECTION 1 — THE ESCAPING EXCEPTION IS NOT A BARE NoRegionError, so this ticket's AC would pass
VACUOUSLY as written. pydantic-ai already catches botocore's NoRegionError at
providers/bedrock.py:463 and re-raises `pydantic_ai.exceptions.UserError`:
    "You must provide a `region_name` or a boto3 client for Bedrock Runtime."
Measured with the env stripped of AWS_REGION/AWS_DEFAULT_REGION/AWS_PROFILE. So an AC asserting "a
TYPED error, not a bare NoRegionError" is already true today and proves nothing. The REAL defect is
narrower and must be stated that way: `UserError` is NOT a subclass of rebar's `LLMError` /
`LLMUnavailableError`, so no `except LLMError` handler in rebar catches it — including the review
bot's fail-closed path — and its message names a pydantic-ai kwarg (`region_name`) rather than
`REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION`. Rewrite the AC to assert the raised type IS `LLMConfigError` (hence
catchable by the existing fail-closed handling) AND that the message names the rebar setting.

CORRECTION 2 — `AWS_REGION` ALONE DOES NOT WORK on this botocore, so the infra fix must not use it.
MEASURED:
    AWS_REGION=us-east-1 only      -> Session().region_name is None -> client() raises NoRegionError
    AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=eu-west-1   -> Session().region_name == 'eu-west-1'
botocore's session-variable table (configprovider.py:74) maps region to AWS_DEFAULT_REGION only;
AWS_REGION appears solely in smart-defaults auto-mode and as an endpoint-ruleset builtin. Two rebar
docstrings are INACCURATE about this and should be corrected as part of this ticket:
bedrock_model.py:50-51 and config.py:19-20 both claim boto3 resolves "AWS_REGION/AWS_DEFAULT_REGION".

CORRECTION 3 — the preflight oracle must be `boto3.session.Session().region_name`, NOT env sniffing.
It is a read-only property resolving the config-file key or the env var; no credentials, no network,
no IMDS; measured at 0.002s. Hand-rolling `os.environ.get("AWS_REGION")` would report a region that
boto3 then refuses (per correction 2). Keep the boto3 import lazy inside the function, per this
module's leaf-import contract.

WHY IMDS IS IRRELEVANT HERE, now with the mechanism: botocore's IMDSRegionProvider is wired ONLY into
the smart-defaults path (defaults_mode=auto), so a reachable IMDS supplies credentials but never a
region. That confirms this ticket's "two independent concerns" claim at the code level.

COLLATERAL FINDING, worth folding into this ticket's value: the review bot's CloudWatch voter metrics
(voter.py:95/110/151/215, four best-effort call sites) silently no-op for the SAME missing-region
reason. Their comments blame IMDS reachability, which the above shows is not the cause. Setting the
region un-breaks voter metrics too — relevant because eb6e's rollback plan depends on a CloudWatch
alarm firing on VOTER_ERROR.

EXACT INFRA TARGET, with a precedent already in the tree: infra/compose/docker-compose.yml, service
`review-bot`, environment block at :88-109. Two services below, the `opcert` service at :157-161
ALREADY sets the region with a comment diagnosing this identical failure ("the region is not
auto-discovered inside the container -> set it explicitly (else the job fails 'You must specify a
region')"). Root cause of the asymmetry: infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh fetches the region from IMDSv2
at :33-40 but only `export`s it into its own shell for the aws CLI calls; the `.env` it writes at
:111-127 contains no region key. So fixing fetch-secrets.sh to emit the region is the alternative
that would cover both services.

TEST HOME AND A TRAP: tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py section C ("construction"), right after
test_missing_bedrock_extra_raises_naming_the_install_command at :306 — same LLMConfigError import,
adjacent shape precedent. The test MUST `monkeypatch.delenv` AWS_DEFAULT_REGION/AWS_REGION/AWS_PROFILE
and set AWS_CONFIG_FILE to os.devnull, or a developer with ~/.aws/config passes it vacuously by
resolving a real region. For the infra assertion, copy tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py:374
(test_opcert_compose_service_sets_aws_region) one service over — and assert AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, per
correction 2.

# The review-bot container resolves NO AWS region — a Bedrock cutover fails at client construction

## MEASURED (from inside `compose-review-bot-1` on i-00880b2c7f13527c5, account 896586841071)

```
env | grep '^AWS_'        -> (nothing: no AWS_REGION, no AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, no keys)
env | grep '^REBAR_LLM_'  -> NO_REBAR_LLM_ENV   (so REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION is unset too)
boto3.session.Session().region_name        -> None
boto3.client('bedrock-runtime')            -> NoRegionError: You must specify a region.
converse(...) with no explicit region      -> NoRegionError: You must specify a region.
```

Every earlier Bedrock probe in this epic passed `region_name="us-east-1"` EXPLICITLY, which is exactly why this went unnoticed — those probes never exercised ambient resolution.

## Why this breaks the cutover

`src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py::build_bedrock_provider` does:

```python
region = cfg.bedrock_region_name or None
return BedrockProvider(region_name=region)
```

`cfg.bedrock_region_name` comes from `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION`, which is UNSET in the container. So `region=None` and `BedrockProvider` falls through to boto3's own resolution — which, as measured, finds nothing and raises `NoRegionError`.

That is a HARD failure at client construction, before any model call, and story eb6e ships the cutover with **NO cross-provider fallback**. So flipping `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` to `bedrock:...` without also setting a region takes the `LLM-Review` gate down for every landing rather than degrading it.

**Notably, IMDS is NOT the region source here.** IMDS is reachable from the container (token PUT returns 200, role resolves — see 9249), yet `session.region_name` is still `None`. So region discovery is ORTHOGONAL to the IMDS/hop-limit contingency: fixing IMDS reachability would not supply a region, and region must be configured explicitly no matter what IMDS does. That distinction matters because it is easy to assume the instance-metadata path covers both.

## Approach (candidate)

Set the region explicitly for the bot service — `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` (rebar's own knob, which `build_bedrock_provider` already threads) or `AWS_REGION` in the container environment. Prefer the rebar knob so the value is visible to rebar's config layer and to `provider_provenance` (343b).

Consider ALSO failing loudly and early: today a missing region surfaces as a boto3 `NoRegionError` from deep inside provider construction. A pre-flight check that names `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` would turn a confusing runtime stack trace into an actionable config error — the same shape as the existing typed `LLMConfigError` for a missing bedrock package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the cutover runbook records the Bedrock region setting and its value
- [ ] [operator-attested] the bot service environment sets an explicit Bedrock region, evidenced by
      container `env` output in a comment
- [ ] a test asserts that building the bedrock provider with NO resolvable region raises a TYPED, actionable rebar error naming the region setting — not a bare boto3 `NoRegionError`
- [ ] [operator-attested] from inside the review-bot container, `boto3.client('bedrock-runtime')` with NO explicit region succeeds after the change, evidenced by command output in a comment
- [ ] the runbook states that IMDS reachability does NOT supply a region, so the hop-limit contingency and region config are independent concerns
compiled_state.title: Bedrock cutover hard-fails with NoRegionError: the review-bot container has no region configured
